elements.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Rendered 28.1 reads: "This Agreement is governed exclusively by the laws of the State of New York." The Singapore choice-of-law wording is fully replaced, and no competing governing-law sentence survives in 28.2 (which addresses forum only).

elements.element: State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction.
elements.evidence: Existing 28.2 is retained verbatim: "The state and federal courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction, and each Party irrevocably submits to personal jurisdiction and waives any objection based on venue or inconvenient forum." The conflicting Singapore exclusive-forum sentence in 28.1 was deleted, so no ambiguity remains; the narrow carve-out for temporary injunctive relief to protect confidential information/IP does not displace exclusive jurisdiction over the merits.

elements.element: The governing law is Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: Rendered 28.1 selects "the laws of the State of New York," not Delaware, California, or England and Wales. Not a defect: the drafter targeted the preferred level, which supersedes this fallback element.

elements.element: The dispute forum is the corresponding Delaware or California courts, or the courts of London for England and Wales law.
elements.evidence: Forum in 28.2 is the state and federal courts in New York County, not Delaware/California courts or the courts of London. Consistent with the preferred target rather than a defect.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: 28.1 as rendered selects New York law and unchanged 28.2 confers exclusive jurisdiction on the state and federal courts in New York County, so both preferred atomic elements are satisfied in operative language rather than only in the margin comment.
The fallback checklist is unmet by design (New York is neither Delaware, California, nor England and Wales); because either level alone suffices, this does not defeat completeness.

Minimal: the edit touches only the jurisdiction words in 28.1 and removes the Singapore exclusive-forum clause that directly contradicted 28.2. No duplicate forum language was inserted, 28.2's favourable submission-to-jurisdiction and venue/inconvenient-forum waiver is retained verbatim, and no obligation outside the GOVLAW checklist (e.g., fee-shifting, jury waiver, service-of-process terms) was added.

Preserves intent: the executive-escalation step in 28.3 and the carve-out permitting temporary injunctive relief in another competent court to protect confidential information or intellectual property survive without contradiction; no arbitration seat is introduced or removed elsewhere, and remedies, timing, and commercial mechanics are untouched.

The internal inconsistency the original document contained (Singapore exclusive jurisdiction in 28.1 versus New York County exclusive jurisdiction in 28.2) is resolved in one direction only, so the rendered clause has a single, non-ambiguous forum.

Finding status "deviation" is correctly applied: the original clause failed the fallback on its material terms and, as an exclusive foreign venue outside the accepted list, sat in walk-away territory, so a redline rather than a rationale note was warranted.
Margin comment is compliant in tone and length, states what changed and why, cites the playbook position, and offers the Delaware/California/England-and-Wales fallback.
